articles.title: February Sky Events and Observing
articles.summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to astronomical events and observing opportunities for February 2009. It includes a calendar highlighting celestial happenings, historical astronomy anniversaries, and educational activities from NASA's Space Place. Additionally, it offers detailed insights into more advanced observations, such as Venus's phases, challenging transits of Saturn's moons (including a rare Titan transit), planetary conjunctions involving Mercury, Jupiter, and Mars, and a subtle penumbral lunar eclipse.

articles.title: Superstar Hide and Seek
articles.summary: Astronomers are actively searching for supermassive stars hidden within the Milky Way, which, despite being millions of times more luminous than the Sun, are obscured by dense dust clouds. The Spitzer Space Telescope, using infrared observations, recently helped identify the Peony nebula star, the second-brightest known star in our galaxy, and researchers estimate dozens to hundreds more such stars might exist. While these stars are ticking bombs poised to go supernova, they pose no immediate threat to Earth due to their distance and the focused nature of gamma-ray bursts.

articles.title: Starry, Starry Night
articles.summary: The article details Almaaz (Epsilon Aurigae), an F-class star known for its extraordinary 27.1-year eclipse caused by a larger, unseen companion star obscured by a massive dust cloud, potentially a protoplanetary system. The most recent eclipse began in 2009, making it a focal point for professional astronomers, with amateur astronomers encouraged to contribute astrometrical measurements during the event, coinciding with the International Year of Astronomy 2009. The phenomenon provides unique insights into stellar systems and their evolution.

articles.title: SJAA Board News and Elections
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) held its annual board elections in February to elect five new directors, with a slate of five candidates nominated, though one later withdrew. The article also details recent leadership changes, including the resignations of the club president and treasurer, and welcomes new board members Greg Claytor and Kevin Roberts to fill vacated seats. The club anticipates a friendly and cohesive new board.

articles.title: The Last Month In Astronomy
articles.summary: This article summarizes recent astronomical news and discoveries from late 2008 to early 2009, detailing significant findings such as lunar oxygen extraction technology, high-velocity stars, new gamma-ray pulsars, and updates on the Milky Way's mass. It also covers ongoing space missions like the Mars rovers' anniversary, the Epoxi spacecraft's boost, and the readiness of the ALMA and Kepler telescopes, concluding with a guide to celestial events for February 2009, including a lunar eclipse and Ceres opposition.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Program
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers a Telescope Loaner Program, a key membership benefit allowing members to try various telescopes and binoculars before purchasing. The program features a diverse inventory, from small refractors to large Dobsonian telescopes and a spectroscope. The article also provides contact information for SJAA officers, staff, and various club services, along with details about its monthly newsletter, the SJAA Ephemeris.
